### Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

When agents run directory listing commands (`ls`, `dir`, `Get-ChildItem -Recurse`), massive generated directories like `node_modules/`, `target/`, `.git/`, `.venv/`, and build artifacts can dump tens of thousands of lines into the terminal stdout. While OpenCode has output truncation limits (`ToolOutput`), raw listings of heavy dependency trees still consume significant token context before truncation kicks in and can push relevant source files out of the model's view.

This PR implements `.gitignore`-aware directory pruning preambles for shell executions:
1. **Preamble Injection (`packages/core/src/shell/preamble.ts`)**:
   - **POSIX shells (`bash`, `zsh`, `sh`)**: Defines a lightweight `ls()` function that passes `--ignore` flags for common heavy directories (`node_modules`, `target`, `.git`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `dist`, `build`) when GNU `ls` is available, with native fallback.
   - **PowerShell (`pwsh`, `powershell`)**: Defines a `Get-ChildItem` wrapper that intercepts `ls`, `dir`, `gci`, and `Get-ChildItem` to prune noisy directories by default, emits a concise notice informing the agent that items were pruned (`[OpenCode:
title: feat(shell): inject directory pruning preamble to eliminate context bloat
